criteria.evidence: At frozen snapshot 89d174d040b90ceeb474576fc53939086084ecbd1466be08f0653a51c13fac1d, I inspected remote.mjs and its frozen SHA-256 ba21914d8a131532ec38c66e40948621da9d81452449024d59ba5a837a10ea89. The adapter validates one identical fetch/push GitHub destination and active auth; pushes only `EXPECTED:refs/heads/BRANCH` without force/tracking/config; creates or edits the exact repository/head/base PR; requires exact head, structured required checks and a fresh CLEAN/MERGEABLE view; invokes `gh pr merge` with `--match-head-commit`; and returns MERGED only after a full merge OID and exact remote-base match. Frozen remote.test.mjs covers unavailable/auth/lookup distinctions, pending/failed/unknown checks, head races, rejected/queued/mismatched merges and already-merged read-only reconciliation using an injected runner. The declared gate passed 340/340 with no failures; test log SHA-256 48c78552418eaa7fa14fb4651b8c78332ab5b65695fdbd1ddf694c4983d4a2f2. No real provider/model call is present in these tests.

Actual CLI functions exist, but the frozen lifecycle does not meet the required proof and pending-state contract. First, current-pm.mjs:324-343 validates only record binding, any slots that happen to exist and a minimal completion tuple; :392-395 releases nonblocking COMPLETE solely when completion.commit is an ancestor of HEAD. It does not require source publication/merge effects, source Git proof, finalized remote-M gates/review/verification, closure/repair proof, or exact retained terminal story/handoff artifacts, so syntactically coherent incomplete evidence can release claims. Second, integration.mjs:2167-2183 sets the rebase range start to the final commit's immediate parent, so it inspects only the final edge: I→U(add unauthorized)→V(revert to I tree)→M(apply exact source delta) can pass without examining U/V, contrary to the whole bounded first-parent contract. Third, source merge recovery at :2074-2077 treats MERGE_PENDING as exact absence and can replay a queued merge; closure and repair provider writes lack the generic executing-attempt reconciliation, with closure stuck as PROVIDER_EXECUTING after a lost process and repair able to allocate another attempt. These violate remote-lifecycle-interface.md:9, :17 and :41-43. Passing gates do not establish these omitted boundaries.

The frozen fake-provider/temporary-Git suite does exercise happy-path publish/readiness/merge, fresh remote-M gates/review/verification, P/E/H, raced closure/H2/S, completion and next-story admission, and the operation map exposes `complete`; npm test passed 340/340 in 563301.498166ms and npm run validate passed, validation log SHA-256 4750e94bf4d841f7f53f054413e9df9e5055fbbb25a1d53edfa18c366a54f89b. Scope is clean across ten authorized changed paths. However, its admission negatives alter only completion.commit or add a copied record and never remove/rebind the required proof chain; its rebase negative uses one unauthorized intermediate whose deletion occurs on the inspected final edge, not a separately reverted earlier edge; and interruption tests cover source slots only. Thus the suite does not exercise the full required lifecycle boundaries, and the inspected source admits premature completion, hidden rebase history and unresolved/duplicated closure or repair provider attempts. Builder recover_t05c, test author correction_regressions and verifier correction_verifier are distinct, but the criterion remains failed on functionality and coverage.
